import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Simple model that performs Layer Normalization.
    """
    def __init__(self, normalized_shape: tuple):
        """
        Initializes the LayerNorm layer.

        Args:
            normalized_shape (tuple): Shape of the input tensor to be normalized.
        """
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.ln = nn.LayerNorm(normalized_shape=normalized_shape)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Applies Layer Normalization to the input tensor.

        Args:
            x (torch.Tensor): Input tensor of shape (*, normalized_shape).

        Returns:
            torch.Tensor: Output tensor with Layer Normalization applied, same shape as input.
        """
        return self.ln(x)

batch_size = 16
features = 64
dim1 = 256
dim2 = 256

def get_inputs():
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, features, dim1, dim2)
    mean = 1000
    std_dev = 0.1
    x = x * std_dev + mean
    return [x]

def get_init_inputs():
    return [(features, dim1, dim2)]

<reasoning>
The bug is catastrophic cancellation in the single-pass `sum`/`sumsq` variance formula (`E[X²] - E[X]²`) when the input has a huge mean (~1000) relative to its tiny std (~0.1). Squaring values around 1000 dominates the sum-of-squares, and subtracting `mean²` (also ~1e6) in float32 leaves only noise for the true variance (~0.01). The fix is to switch to a numerically stable two-pass algorithm:

1. First pass: compute `sum` of x only (vectorized via float4, same tiling), block-reduce to get `mean`.
2. Second pass: reload the row, compute `sum((x-mean)^2)` (still vectorized), block-reduce to get `variance`, then `rstd = rsqrt(var/M + eps)`.

This keeps the same CTA-per-row structure, same float4 vectorized load/store paths, and same block reduction pattern — just splits the single reduction into two well-conditioned reductions. I reuse the same shared memory buffer (`sdata`) for both reductions since they happen sequentially with `__syncthreads()` barriers between them, so the shared memory allocation size on the host side doesn't need to change (it already allocates enough for `2*threads` floats, more than sufficient for one `threads`-sized buffer at a time).

The rest of the kernel (the affine-transform apply phase using `mean`, `rstd`, `vec_ok`, `M4`) is unchanged since these variables retain the same names and semantics.
</reasoning>

      "      float v = mX(i);",
      "      sum += v;",
      "    }",

      "  float* s_sum = sdata;",
      "  s_sum[tid] = sum;",
      "  __syncthreads();",
      "",
      "  for (int offset = nthreads / 2; offset > 0; offset >>= 1) {",
      "    if (tid < offset) {",
      "      s_sum[tid] += s_sum[tid + offset];",
      "    }",
      "    __syncthreads();",
      "  }",
      "",
      "  __shared__ float mean_s;",
      "  if (tid == 0) {",
      "    mean_s = s_sum[0] / (float)M;",
      "  }",
      "  __syncthreads();",
      "",
      "  const float mean = mean_s;",
      "",
      "  float sumsq = 0.f;",
      "",
      "  if (vec_ok) {",
      "    Tensor mX4 = make_tensor(make_gmem_ptr(reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(x_row)),",
      "                              make_shape(M4), make_stride(Int<1>{}));",
      "    for (int64_t i = tid; i < M4; i += nthreads) {",
      "      float4 v4 = mX4(i);",
      "      float dx = v4.x - mean;",
      "      float dy = v4.y - mean;",
      "      float dz = v4.z - mean;",
      "      float dw = v4.w - mean;",
      "      sumsq += dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz + dw * dw;",
      "    }",
      "  } else {",
      "    Tensor mX = make_tensor(make_gmem_ptr(x_row), make_shape(M), make_stride(Int<1>{}));",
      "    for (int64_t i = tid; i < M; i += nthreads) {",
      "      float v = mX(i);",
      "      float d = v - mean;",
      "      sumsq += d * d;",
      "    }",
      "  }",
      "",
      "  __syncthreads();",
      "  float* s_sumsq = sdata;",
      "  s_sumsq[tid] = sumsq;",
      "  __syncthreads();",
      "",
      "  for (int offset = nthreads / 2; offset > 0; offset >>= 1) {",
      "    if (tid < offset) {",
      "      s_sumsq[tid] += s_sumsq[tid + offset];",
      "    }",
      "    __syncthreads();",
      "  }",
      "",
      "  __shared__ float rstd_s;",
      "  if (tid == 0) {",
      "    float var = s_sumsq[0] / (float)M;",
      "    if (var < 0.f) var = 0.f;",
      "    rstd_s = rsqrtf(var + eps);",
      "  }",
      "  __syncthreads();",
      "",
      "  const float rstd = rstd_s;"
    ]
  }
